Appellant has filed this first criminal appeal under Section 14-A (1 & 2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 against the order dated 17.01.2023 passed by Special Judge(Atrocities), Shahdol whereby bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of appellant has been dismissed by the trial Court.

sentences.text: Looking to the nature of allegation, it appears that both appellant and prosecutrix lived in physical proximity for last two years and as per allegations on the pretext of marriage, appellant gained physical proximity.
Statement of the prosecutrix u/s 164 of Cr.P.C indicates consensual nature of relationship.
Confinement amounts to pretrial detention.
He undertakes to cooperate in trial and would not to be a source of harassment or embarrassment to the complainant party in any manner and that he will not move in her vicinity.
On these grounds prayer for bail is made out.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and prayed for rejection of appeal.
Counsel for the Objector/complainant extends no objection if bail is granted to the appellant.
Heard.

Considering the submissions and fact situation and looking to the 164 statement of the prosecutrix,
without commenting on the merits of case, appeal is allowed and it is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand only)
with two solvent sureties of like amount to the satisfaction of Trial Court.

The appellant will not indulge himself in extending inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to the Police Officer, as the case may be;

opennyai_summary.facts:
Appellant has filed this first criminal appeal under Section 14-A (1 & 2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 against the order dated 17.01.2023 passed by Special Judge(Atrocities), Shahdol whereby bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of appellant has been dismissed by the trial Court.

1 506 of IPC and section 3(1)(w)
(i) and 3 (2) (v-a) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
I t is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that he is suffering confinement since 08.01.2023 on false pretext of marriage.
Looking to the nature of allegation, it appears that both appellant and prosecutrix lived in physical proximity for last two years and as per allegations on the pretext of marriage, appellant gained physical proximity.
Statement of the prosecutrix u/s 164 of Cr.P.C indicates consensual nature of relationship.
Confinement amounts to pretrial detention.
He undertakes to cooperate in trial and would not to be a source of harassment or embarrassment to the complainant party in any manner and that he will not move in her vicinity.
opennyai_summary.decision:
On these grounds prayer for bail is made out.
Counsel for the Objector/complainant extends no objection if bail is granted to the appellant.
Considering the submissions and fact situation and looking to the 164 statement of the prosecutrix,
without commenting on the merits of case, appeal is allowed and it is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand only)
with two solvent sureties of like amount to the satisfaction of Trial Court.
This order will remain operative subject to compliance of the following conditions by the appellant :-
1.The appellant will comply with all the terms and conditions of the bond executed by him;
2. The appellant will cooperate in the investigation/trial, as the case may be;
3.
The appellant will not indulge himself in extending inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to the Police Officer, as the case may be;
4. The appellant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused;
5. Applicant shall not move in the vicinity of prosecutrix and shall not be a source of embarrassment and harassment to her in any manner and shall not try to contact the prosecutrix in person, through electronic/social media mode or somebody else,
